text.p: Shares ended a lively session modestly higher on Friday as insurance companies continued to benefit from speculation about a possible shake-up in the Finnish financial services sector.
The HEX index rose 0.35 percent to 2,171.00, its highest since early October 1995. The HEX was up 1.5 percent for the week. Volume was fairly sound at 358 million markka.
Brokers said insurers were lifted not only by the talk of an insurance sector reshuffle, but also by expectations that recent gains in stocks and bonds would boost their earnings.
Among insurers, Pohjola advanced 1.70 markka to 92.80, and Sampo added 6.00 to close at a two year-high 328 markka.
But brokers said the generally upbeat tone was muffled by Nokia's early losses on Wall Street, which took Nokia 0.10 markka lower to 202.40 after moderate trade in Helsinki.
Nokia accounted for 28 percent of total bourse turnover.

Beverages group Hartwall extended gains after reporting strong January-August profits on Thursday. It closed active trade 9.00 markka higher at 143.00 after touching but failing to hold a new all-time high 148.00.
Steel group Rautaruukki shed 0.10 markka to close at 39.50, in what brokers called a mild reaction to the company's profit-warning issued on Friday.
Forestries remained soft, with the sub-index weakening 0.76 percent. Metsa-Serla, which warned of lower profits on Tuesday, fell 0.50 markka to 29.50.
